body:
Nick Halloway (snowe@rain.org) wrote:

: The complaints mentioned are things that make the lives of women, gays,
: colored people hard.  The concept of "PC" was about conformism among
: leftists, which is different.  I get tired of "PC" being used to tar
: any quest for fairness.

: Also, his idea that people should drop their fight against discrimination
: feels *wrong*.  Women in leftist causes were often told this by the men,
: to drop any idea of fighting for their own rights because the "greater 
: cause" was more important.  But telling people to "swallow their
: grudges" isn't a great idea and it would be unlikely to be helpful
: if they did.  Tk would have first to convince people of the validity of
: his ideas anyways, and people are far from convinced.  And, I think it
: may be more that all the problems people perceive fit *together* -- 
: patriarchy, consumerism, racism, technology becoming a substitute world.
: Shutting out other ways of seeing problems seems wrong.  
:
: And, anybody feels their cause is important.  A lot of people would 
: argue that one thing is at the *root* of the problems in civilization:
: that the way children are treated is the foundation of our problems, 
: that the oppression of women is *the* fundamental problem.  Kaczynski
: isn't alone in claiming that *his* cause is what attention should be
: paid to.  

Agreed.  TK has the big picture in mind, but has trouble communicating
it clearly.  

TK writes:
: "Ahem. You all have good reasons to complain. But it seems
: to me that what we really have to do is get this ship turned
: around and headed back south, because if we keep going north
: we're sure to be wrecked sooner or later, and then your
: wages, your blankets, and your right to suck cocks won't do
: you any good, because we'll all drown."

His plea that "we'll all drown" seems ridiculous to the others.  When
people look around in our society, they don't automatically think
"hey, we're gonna drown".  And when is "sooner or later"?  Who cares!

So why does no one notice?  The boat is moving slowly... 

In the 159th paragraph of the gospel according to TK, he writes:
: Will public resistance prevent the introduction of
: technological control of human behavior? It certainly would
: if an attempt were made to introduce such control all at
: once. But since technological control will be introduced
: through a long sequence of small advances, there will be no
: rational and effective public resistance. (See paragraphs
: 127,132,153.)

People generally don't see the big picture or overall direction of 
things and I don't believe the cabin boy opened their eyes to it.
It wasn't laid out piece by piece:

1.  You are helping move this boat forward.
2.  The boat is heading north.
3.  If it wasn't heading north, you wouldn't be cold or hungry and 
    if you weren't working on the boat you wouldn't be restricted in your
    languages or enjoyment of sex.
     
But the people need jobs.  That's what they see.  Who are they to
argue with the big issues of the existence of the boat and it's
direction?  It's tough to get people to look further than their ass.
 
: Also, targeting oppressed groups trying to get equal rights seems so 
: misguided.  Feminists, civil rights leaders, etc. aren't the problem.
: They are likely themselves to be more conscious of environmental issues
: than others.  The problem is more like massive complacency and denial,
: and human nature that makes people go for the toys technology gives 
: them, and ignore the poverty of other countries.  

Agreed.  People also have a difficult time recognizing that their
supposed freedom (in the form of car for example) can also be enslaving.
How are your car payments?  How many days of the year fo you work to
pay for your car?  But alas... it's our God-given right to drive!  Ugh.

Paragraph 125: "Technology Is A More Powerful Social Force
Than The Aspiration For Freedom"

: There seems to be massive denial about global warming, for example.  
: It looks pretty sure that we're heading into an increasingly severe
: environmental crisis with CO2 and CFC's in the atmosphere, and that
: if we don't do something there are _really_ going to be problems in
: 25-50 years or so -- a lot of species dying out because they can't 
: relocate fast enough for the climate change, a lot of flooding, 
: high temperatures, 50% or so less rainfall in most countries, etc.  
: Really massive problems.  Yet the last I heard the Senate isn't 
: apparently ratifying the Kyoto protocol to cut back carbon dioxide 
: emissions, SUV's are very popular, people don't seem to be changing
: things.  It looks like people are likely to go on more or less 
: doing what they do, with a world population going towards 10 billion
: and more and more cars around, heating up the planet, and will just
: let whatever happens happen.

I've read that 2-cycle engines (lawnmowers, most outboard boat
engines and motorcycles and jetskis and snowmobiles) are orders of
magnitude worse than automobile engines.  Maybe these would be a
better target.  Who was complaining about lawns recently?

I've also just read that sulfur from ships has helped reduce global
warming.   It causes clouds along the shipping routes which reflects
sun back.  I think the researchers said it's probably helped by 2-3 C
over the century according to their models.  

Crazy world.

: The problem isn't feminism or civil rights leaders etc., it's 
: lack of foresight and selfishness.  

The treament of "Ship of Fools" on NPR on 2/24 ATC was interesting.
It seemed like the overall points of TK got thru better than during
coverage of the manifesto which just got called boring or dry or
difficult or whatever.  Plus, the fact that he killed is old news so
they didn't spend much time talking about that.

http://www.cs.umass.edu/~ehaugsja/unabom/ship.html

E
